environment.fallback.timeout: Reading the login shell timed out, so a fallback PATH from known folders is used.
environment.fallback.exit: The login shell exited with an error, so a fallback PATH is used.
environment.fallback.no_markers: The login shell did not print the whole environment, so a fallback PATH is used.
environment.fallback.spawn_failed: The login shell could not be started, so a fallback PATH is used.
environment.tool.status.mismatch: Needs setup: version {required} is required, {available} is available
environment.tool.status.missing: Needs setup: the tool is not installed
environment.tool.status.unknown: The version is unknown until the version check
environment.tool.proposed: A matching version is installed by {manager}, proposed explicitly in the standards profile: {path}
environment.tool.corepack: {tool} here is a corepack shim, which may download the declared version. It is checked without the network; if that version is missing, the check needs setup.
environment.tool.shellFunction: In your terminal “{tool}” is a shell function (nvm), so it runs {terminal} there, while PATH gives {path}.
